title: What the Multi-Tenant Portal Tenant Details page shows for a tenant: subscriptions, limits, defaults, API keys, clusters, contacts and Executive Insights

prose.text: {{dc-exclusion}} {{custom-cloud-app}} {{auth-service-flags}} {{and-urlcat-jwt}} {{schedule-qbr}} {{saas-collaborator-count}} Limited RBA and SMAA Servers have only a one-line description {{gap:unexplained-rows}}.

view-only.statement: The Tenant Details page is view-only and cannot be modified within the Multi-Tenant Portal; configuration changes go through Zscaler Support.

quotes: This information is view-only and cannot be modified within the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for partners. If you want to make changes to your configurations, contact Zscaler Support.

view-on.statement: The View On control gives access to the tenant's ZIA Admin Portal, and to other admin portals such as ZDX and Zscaler Cloud Connector if the tenant is provisioned on them.

quotes: View On: Hover over to access the ZIA Admin Portal of the tenant account. You can also access other admin portals (i.e., Digital Experience (ZDX), Zscaler Cloud Connector, etc.) if the tenant is provisioned on them.

general-fields.statement: General account information includes the Primary Account Owner, Tenant Since, the Internal Domain (generated when the tenant account is created with Zscaler) and the CMC Hostname associated with the tenant.

quotes: Primary Account Owner: The owner of the tenant account.
Tenant Since: The date since the organization has been Zscaler's tenant.
Internal Domain: The internal domain. This domain is generated when the tenant account is created with Zscaler.
CMC Hostname: The CMC Hostname associated with the tenant.

show-partner-logo.statement: Show Partner Logo is a white labeling indicator of whether the partner logo is enabled or disabled in the admin portals the tenant has access to.

quotes: Show Partner Logo: This is a white labeling feature that indicates if the partner logo is enabled or disabled in the admin portals the tenant has access to.

subscription-status.statement: A subscription's Status is one of on trial, expired, not subscribed, subscribed or temporarily extended, and the ADD-ON tag beside a service name marks an additional service included in the package.

quotes: Status: Whether the subscription package is on trial, expired, not subscribed, subscribed, or temporarily extended.
The ADD-ON tag beside the service name indicates the additional service included in the package.

subscription-columns.statement: The subscription list shows each service's SKU (the ID of the service) and the Number of Licenses the tenant owns.

quotes: SKU: The ID of the service.
Number of Licenses: The number of licenses the tenant owns.

self-provisioned-ip.statement: The Self-provisioned IP Limit shown for a tenant is 100, 1,000, 10K, or 100K; Self-service GRE and IP Provisioning, if enabled, lets the tenant provision GRE or IP addresses in the ZIA Admin Portal.

quotes: Self-provisioned IP Limit: Indicates the self-provisioning IP limit in the ZIA Admin Portal. The limit is 100, 1,000, 10K, or 100K.
Self-service GRE and IP Provisioning: If enabled, allows the tenant to provision GRE or IP addresses in the ZIA Admin Portal.

custom-url-category-limit.statement: The Custom URL Category Limit shown for a tenant indicates the number of URL categories configurable in the ZIA Admin Portal and can be either 56 or 256.

quotes: Custom URL Category Limit: Indicates the number of URL categories that can be configured in the ZIA Admin Portal. It can be either 56 or 256.

custom-file-type-limit.statement: The Custom File Type Limit shown for a tenant is the number of custom file types for file type policies and can be 512, 1,024 or 2,048; the default value is blank.

quotes: Custom File Type Limit: Indicates the number of custom file types that can be created for file type policies in the ZIA Admin Portal. It can either be 512, 1,024, or 2,048. The default value is blank.

pac-limits.statement: Large PAC Files (up to 2MB) indicates whether 2MB PAC files are supported, against a normal limit of 256 KB; PAC Files up to 1K raises the per-organization maximum to 1,000 (1,024 PAC files) when enabled and is 256 when disabled.

quotes: Large PAC Files (up to 2MB): Indicates whether 2MB PAC files are supported or not. The normal limit is up to 256 KB.

PAC Files up to 1K: When enabled, the maximum limit of PAC files per organization is increased to 1,000 (i.e., 1,024 PAC files). When disabled, the maximum number of PAC files allowed per organization is 256.

sandbox-fields.statement: Tenant details list the Sandbox Cluster, where files are quarantined and scanned for malicious activities, plus daily limits for sandbox unique files analyzed and for sandbox API file submissions.

quotes: Sandbox Cluster: The cluster where files are quarantined and scanned for malicious activities.
Sandbox Unique Files Analyzed Daily Limit: The daily file limit for sandbox analysis.
Sandbox API File Submission Daily Limit: The daily API file limit for sandbox analysis.

clusters.statement: Tenant details list the Preferred Nanolog Cluster where tenant logs are recorded, the SMCDSS DLP Cluster used for Exact Data Match schema files, and the Nanolog cluster for logs forwarded from Virtual Service Edge.

quotes: Preferred Nanolog Cluster: The cluster where the tenant logs are recorded.
SMCDSS DLP Cluster: The cluster where the ADP client uploads or downloads the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Schema files for Exact Data Match (EDM).
Nanolog cluster to forward logs from Virtual Service Edge: This field shows where the tenant's Virtual Service Edge (Virtual ZEN (VZEN)) logs are directed and saved.

nss-multiplier.statement: The NSS Subscriptions Multiplier shows the number of NSS for a tenant; for example, a value of 8 means the customer can configure 8 different NSS of each type.

quotes: NSS Subscriptions Multiplier: This field shows the number of NSS for a tenant. For example, if set to 8, the customer can configure 8 different NSS of each type.

dc-exclusion.statement: DC Exclusion, if enabled, restricts customer data forwarding to all data centers within the country, and DC Exclusion for Traffic Forwarding shows the Traffic Forwarding Method option for DC Exclusion in the ZIA Admin Portal.

quotes: DC Exclusion: If enabled, restricts customer data forwarding to all data centers (DCs) within the country.

DC Exclusion for Traffic Forwarding: When enabled, it shows the Traffic Forwarding Method option for DC Exclusion in the ZIA Admin Portal (Administration > Resources > DC Exclusion > Traffic Forwarding Method).

edm-duplicates.statement: EDM Primary Key Max Duplicates across Schemas, when enabled, indicates the number of supported duplicate primary keys for a schema file, with a maximum of 512.

quotes: EDM Primary Key Max Duplicates across Schemas: When enabled, indicates the number of supported duplicate primary keys for a schema file. The maximum can be 512.

high-group-limit.statement: High Group Limit indicates whether a user can belong to more than 100 groups; if enabled, the limit is up to 128.

quotes: High Group Limit: Indicates whether the user can belong to more than 100 groups. If enabled, the limit is up to 128.

cloud-app-instances.statement: A customer can create up to 512 cloud application instances, and a maximum of 1,024 keyword type identifiers per cloud application instance is allowed, each no longer than 128 characters.

quotes: A customer can create up to 512 cloud application instances.
A maximum of 1,024 keyword type identifiers per cloud application instance is allowed. The length of the identifier should not exceed 128 characters.

custom-filehash.statement: Custom Filehash lets customers configure their own custom file blocklists based on MD5 hashes in the ZIA Admin Portal, up to a maximum of 10K MD5 hashes.

quotes: Custom Filehash: When enabled, it allows customers to configure their own custom file blocklists based on MD5 hashes in the ZIA Admin Portal. Customers can block up to a maximum of 10K MD5 hashes.

custom-cloud-app.statement: Custom Cloud App Support, when enabled, allows customers to configure their own applications in the ZIA Admin Portal and cannot be disabled if any custom cloud applications have been added to a tenant.

quotes: Custom Cloud App Support: When enabled, it allows customers to configure their own applications in the ZIA Admin Portal. This cannot be disabled if any custom cloud applications have been added to a tenant.

auth-service-flags.statement: The Authentication Service Admin and Authentication Service User options, when enabled, allow admin or user access to the Authentication Service Admin Portal; by default, both are disabled.

quotes: Authentication Service Admin: When enabled, it allows admin access to the Authentication Service Admin Portal and the Managed ZID link becomes visible. By default, this option is disabled.
Authentication Service User: When enabled, it allows users to access the Authentication Service Admin Portal. By default, this option is disabled.

and-urlcat-jwt.statement: AND Functionality for URL Filtering Categories and JWT Auth for Workload are options shown on tenant details, each disabled by default.

quotes: AND Functionality for URL Filtering Categories: When enabled, it provides the support for the logical operation AND between the URL categories in a URL filtering rule in the ZIA Admin Portal. By default, this option is disabled.

JWT Auth for Workload: When enabled, it provides support for JWT authentication for workload locations under Administration > Location Management in the ZIA Admin Portal. By default, this option is disabled.

api-keys.statement: Tenant details show an API Key for the public ZIA APIs, a Sandbox API Key for the Sandbox APIs, and an EC API Key for the public EC APIs, each shown if generated.

quotes: API Key: This field shows the API key used for accessing the public ZIA APIs, if generated.
Sandbox API Key: This field shows the API key used for accessing the Sandbox APIs, if generated.
EC API Key: This field shows the EC API key used for accessing the public EC APIs, if generated.

password-reset-emails.statement: Activation details show whether the ZIA, ZDX, Zscaler Cloud Connector, ZCSPM Admin, BI and Risk Analytics password reset emails are enabled or disabled, and the Activation Email Recipient receives the activation or password reset email for the enabled fields.

quotes: Send ZIA Password Reset Email: Indicates whether sending the ZIA password reset email is enabled or disabled.
Send ZDX Password Reset Email: Indicates whether sending the Digital Experience (ZDX) password reset email is enabled or disabled.
Send Zscaler Cloud Connector Password Reset Email: Indicates whether sending the Zscaler Cloud Connector password reset email is enabled or disabled.
Send ZCSPM Admin Password Reset Email: Indicates whether sending the Zscaler Cloud Security Posture Management (ZCSPM) password reset email is enabled or disabled.
Send BI Password Reset Email: Indicates whether sending the password reset link email notification to the Zscaler Business Intelligence (BI) contact is enabled or disabled.
Send Risk Analytics Password Reset Email: Indicates whether sending the password reset link email notification to the Zscaler Risk Analytics contact is enabled or disabled.
Activation Email Recipient: The email ID of the recipient to receive the activation or password reset email for enabled preceding fields.

executive-insights.statement: Executive Insights must be enabled for the tenant account to receive the Insights reports; details show the addresses receiving the report at generation and 7 days after, and the allowed external email domains.

quotes: The Executive Insights must be enabled for the tenant account in order to receive the Insights reports.
Send at report generation: The email addresses that receive the Executive Insights Report when it's generated.
Send after 7 days: The email addresses that receive the Executive Insights Report 7 days from the date of the report generation.
Allowed external email domains: Displays the external email domains allowed to receive the Executive Insights Report.

schedule-qbr.statement: Schedule QBR generates the Quarterly Business Report (QBR) every quarter, if configured.

quotes: Schedule QBR: This option generates the Quarterly Business Report (QBR) every quarter, if configured.

saas-collaborator-count.statement: SaaS Security Collaborator Count, when enabled, specifies the number of users who can access certain files in a SaaS application.

quotes: SaaS Security Collaborator Count: When enabled, this knob specifies the number of users who can access certain files in a SaaS application.

contacts.statement: Tenant details show primary and secondary contacts for Billing, Technical or Business divisions and, if provisioned, for ZDX, Zscaler Cloud Connector, Zscaler Deception, Zscaler Risk Analytics, BI and ZCSPM, with an alternate phone number for a contact if any.

quotes: The primary and secondary contact details for Billing, Technical, or Business divisions, and if provisioned, you can view the contact information for ZDX, Zscaler Cloud Connector, Zscaler Deception, Zscaler Risk Analytics, Zscaler Business Intelligence (BI), and Zscaler Cloud Security Posture Management (ZCSPM).
Alternate Phone: The alternate phone number of the contact person, if any.

custom-url-category-count.summary: The Tenant Details page gives the Custom URL Category Limit as 56 or 256, while the ZIA pages give 64 custom categories, raisable to 1,024 through Zscaler Support.

positions.says: The Custom URL Category Limit is either 56 or 256.

quotes: Custom URL Category Limit: Indicates the number of URL categories that can be configured in the ZIA Admin Portal. It can be either 56 or 256.

positions.says: Up to 64 custom categories can be created, and Zscaler Support can raise the limit to a maximum of 1,024.

quotes: The default limit for custom categories is 64.
Contact Zscaler Support to increase the limit to a maximum of 1,024 categories.

custom-url-category-count.impact: A tenant showing 56 or 256 does not match the 64 default the ZIA pages state, and neither set of pages says how the two relate.

group-limit.summary: The Tenant Details page says a High Group Limit flag raises the per-user group limit from 100 to 128, while the ZIA pages give 127 by default and 128 without mentioning such a flag.

positions.says: High Group Limit indicates whether the user can belong to more than 100 groups; if enabled, the limit is up to 128.

quotes: High Group Limit: Indicates whether the user can belong to more than 100 groups. If enabled, the limit is up to 128.

positions.says: The limits table gives 127 groups per user by default.

quotes: | Groups per User | 127 groups by default |

positions.says: The SCIM article says the total number of groups associated with a single user cannot exceed 128.

quotes: In addition, the total number of groups associated with a single user cannot exceed 128.

group-limit.impact: Whether a tenant without High Group Limit enabled is capped at 100, 127 or 128 groups per user is not stated.

cloud-app-instance-limit.summary: The Tenant Details page says a customer can create up to 512 cloud application instances, while the ZIA limits page gives 512 with a possible increase to 4,096 through Zscaler Support and 2,048 identifiers across all instances.

positions.says: A customer can create up to 512 cloud application instances, with a maximum of 1,024 keyword identifiers per instance.

quotes: A customer can create up to 512 cloud application instances.
A maximum of 1,024 keyword type identifiers per cloud application instance is allowed.

positions.says: 512 cloud application instances, with a possible increase to 4,096 through Zscaler Support, and at most 2,048 instance identifiers across all instances.

quotes: | Cloud Application Instance | 512 cloud application instances | Contact Zscaler Support for a possible increase in the limit of cloud application instances from 512 to 4,096. |
There can be a maximum of 2,048 instance identifiers across all instances.

cloud-app-instance-limit.impact: The Tenant Details page states 512 as the ceiling, and does not reconcile 1,024 identifiers per instance with the 2,048 total across all instances.

edm-duplicate-scope.summary: The Tenant Details page gives the EDM primary key duplicate maximum as 512 across schemas, while the ZIA EDM article gives 512 for an individual template and 2,048 across multiple templates.

positions.says: EDM Primary Key Max Duplicates across Schemas has a maximum of 512.

quotes: EDM Primary Key Max Duplicates across Schemas: When enabled, indicates the number of supported duplicate primary keys for a schema file. The maximum can be 512.

positions.says: 512 duplicate keys for an individual EDM template and 2,048 across multiple EDM templates.

quotes: All of the examples use the 512 duplicate key limit for an individual EDM template and the 2,048 duplicate key limit across multiple EDM templates.

edm-duplicate-scope.impact: The 512 labelled as across schemas is a per-template figure on the ZIA page, and it is not stated which scope the Tenant Details field sets.

view-only-wording.summary: The Tenant Details page says its information cannot be modified within the portal, while the account settings page says you can make changes to the information associated with your tenant's account.

positions.says: Tenant Details information is view-only and cannot be modified within the portal; changes go through Zscaler Support.

quotes: This information is view-only and cannot be modified within the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

positions.says: You can make changes to the information associated with your tenant's account.

quotes: You can make changes to the information associated with your tenant's account.

view-only-wording.impact: The account settings sentence is under the page for the partner's own account settings, so which tenant information it means is not stated.

unexplained-rows.title: What the unexplained Tenant Details rows mean
unexplained-rows.detail: Limited RBA is described only as indicating whether the number Role-Based Access is limited, and SMAA Servers only as the configured SMAA servers for the tenant account; neither article line gives values or what the limit or servers affect.
